scope: Diagnosis of ordinary-v1 body/neck/clothing mismatch and acceptance criteria for ordinary-v2. V1 assets untouched.
priorQaCorrection: Previous visual QA incorrectly accepted absence of transparent gaps as evidence of anatomical fit. Contact-sheet and tiny-UI review hid the collar/neck geometry and shoulder-scale mismatch. The previous 'passed' assessment was insufficient for body/clothing fit.

groundTruth.evidence: V1 garment() selects one unisex garment per wardrobe and stage; garmentId contains no sex/body reference. All six faces are pasted onto unrelated generated torso silhouettes.

groundTruth.issue: Bounding boxes are not neck registration
groundTruth.evidence: normalise() independently fits head and garment alpha bounding boxes to separate envelopes, bottom-aligns each, and writes a nominal [400,700] anchor. It never measures or constrains the actual throat, collar, clavicles or shoulder joints.

groundTruth.issue: Original long neck covers the front collar
groundTruth.evidence: assemble() composites garment, then the complete head-and-neck component last. There is no foreground collar mask; the generated neck's flat lower edge is allowed to replace garment neckline pixels.

groundTruth.issue: Wardrobe swaps alter apparent torso width
groundTruth.evidence: All adult garments fit375px height; independent source aspect ratios produce widths582â€“704px. At canvas y800 visible width ranges523â€“634px (work vs everyday). At y900 commerce spans441px vs everyday689px. These are garment raster spans, not anatomical shoulder measurements, but demonstrate uncontrolled scale variation.

v2ConstructionRequirements: Exactly two named canonical body geometry families M/F, each with fixed torso pose, neck, clavicles, shoulder joints and waist anchors. Six face identities are independent of these two body shapes.
Use36 source-specific native eye/chin landmarks for uniform head registration. Remove source skin below jaw before assembly. Never scale a whole long-neck source to fit a shirt opening.
Body neck extends behind jaw; identity skin tone is applied inside a fixed body skin mask without changing body geometry. A different skin tone does not create a new body type.

Each clothing family is authored against the same corresponding M/F template. Match anatomical collar and shoulder landmarks, not outer raster bounding boxes. Garment drape can differ, but underlying shoulder placement and torso pose remain fixed.
Explicitly separate garment rear/body layer and foreground collar. Foreground collar occludes lower neck skin; it must not cross the jaw or cut the throat at an unnatural horizontal line.
Preserve braids and side buns using original hair masks. Inspect for preserved neck-skin spikes inside hair-protection polygons.
Age proportions require deliberate stage treatment within each M/F body family. Do not put infant heads on adult shoulders, or treat an adult body shrunk uniformly as anatomically age-appropriate.
